appraisal_events.evidence: il lui mentait tout le temps, et son esprit de duplicité... était perpétuellement découvert... il ne croyait pouvoir s'en tirer qu'en exagérant dans des proportions ridicules la tristesse réelle qu'il avait de peiner Gilberte; sanglotait, s'inondait d'eau froide, parlait de sa mort prochaine, quelquefois s'abattait sur le parquet.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly exposes Saint-Loup's chronic lying and ridiculous theatrical excess toward Gilberte, diminishing him even though his underlying attachment to her is affirmed as genuine.

appraisal_events.evidence: je vis qu'elle était complètement peinte. C'était cela qui lui faisait cette bouche sanglante... tandis que l'heure du train qui s'approchait sans que Gilberte sût si son mari arrivait vraiment... pâlissait ses joues et cernait ses yeux.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's close, unflattering observation exposes Gilberte's desperate cosmetic self-transformation and visible strain as she anxiously awaits an uncertain husband, locally diminishing her composure and dignity.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's direct exposure of his habitual lying and theatrical excess lowers how Saint-Loup is regarded in this passage, despite an underlying real affection for Gilberte.
Gilberte is left in continual uncertainty by Robert's lies and, in the closing scene, is shown visibly strained and resorting to concealment while anxiously awaiting whether he will even arrive.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's tearful letters and staged scenes are framed as lies, yet the narrator states their emotional content was 'en somme vrai' (basically true), which qualifies but does not reverse the passage's negative framing of his duplicity.
